final_message:
Reproduced the bug on the pinned revision (495e1d3).

Added `helpflag_parallel_test.go`: `TestHelpFlagParallelNilDeref` spawns 32 goroutines, each constructing a `Command` and calling `Run` 20 times. It panics within milliseconds:

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x18]

github.com/urfave/cli/v3.(*FlagBase[...]).Get(...)  flag_impl.go:192
github.com/urfave/cli/v3.(*Command).Value(...)     command.go:533
github.com/urfave/cli/v3.(*Command).Bool(...)      flag_bool.go:28
slices.ContainsFunc[...](...)
github.com/urfave/cli/v3.(*Command).checkHelp(...) command.go:186
github.com/urfave/cli/v3.(*Command).run(...)       command_run.go:198
```

The crash path matches the report: `checkHelp` calls `cmd.Bool("help")` -> `flag.Get()`, which dereferences `f.value`; meanwhile another goroutine's `ensureHelp` (`command_setup.go:202-211`) mutates the shared global `HelpFlag`, setting `hf.value = nil`.

Note: no Go toolchain was preinstalled; I installed go1.24.4 to `~/gotoolchain` (outside the repo, not in the patch).

Run command from repo root: `go test -run TestHelpFlagParallelNilDeref -count=200 -failfast .`
patch:
diff --git a/helpflag_parallel_test.go b/helpflag_parallel_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f847470
--- /dev/null
+++ b/helpflag_parallel_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
+package cli
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"sync"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+// Reproduces https://github.com/urfave/cli/issues/2176:
+// ensureHelp resets the shared global HelpFlag's internal state
+// (hf.value = nil) while another goroutine is parsing it,
+// causing a nil pointer dereference.
+func TestHelpFlagParallelNilDeref(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	const workers = 32
+
+	run := func() {
+		cmd := &Command{
+			Name:  "debug",
+			Usage: "make an explosive entrance",
+			Action: func(_ context.Context, _ *Command) error {
+				return nil
+			},
+		}
+		_ = cmd.Run(context.Background(), []string{"debug"})
+	}
+
+	var wg sync.WaitGroup
+	for i := 0; i < workers; i++ {
+		wg.Add(1)
+		go func() {
+			defer wg.Done()
+			for j := 0; j < 20; j++ {
+				run()
+			}
+		}()
+	}
+	wg.Wait()
+}
